subject: Planned capacity rebalancing & microcode security update — us-east4 (2026-08-03)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cloud Ops <cloudops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Planned capacity rebalancing & microcode security update — us-east4 (2026-08-03)

Hi team,

We're reaching out to let you know about a planned maintenance activity in the us-east4 region that will take place on Tuesday, 2026-08-03 between 02:00–05:00 UTC. This work is a coordinated capacity rebalancing across a subset of node pools combined with a microcode security update that patches a CPU vulnerability detected during routine firmware scans.

What to expect
- Impact window: 02:00–05:00 UTC on 2026-08-03.
- Scope: staggered rolling restarts across node pools serving the us-east4 region; traffic will be shifted automatically and we expect minimal request drops.
- Expected customer-facing impact: transient request retries and < 1% increase in tail latency during rolling swaps. No model state or data will be changed.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to warm standby pools in us-east3 if any node pool fails health checks.

Action for Acme
- No action required for normal operations. If you are running pinned single-node instances or have aggressive affinity rules, please reply and we'll review exemptions.

Attachments: status-page-notes.md (summary for your ops playbook)

We'll post live updates on our status page and send a completion note when the window closes. If you have blackout windows or special requests, reply to this thread and we'll prioritize adjustments.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

---
From: Cloud Ops <cloudops@acme-corp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned capacity rebalancing & microcode security update — us-east4 (2026-08-03)

Thanks Olga — appreciate the heads up. A couple quick questions: 
1) Our inference clients have several long-running pipelines that pin a single model replica for affinity (to reduce cold-start sampling noise). Will those be evicted automatically during the rolling restarts?
2) Can you confirm whether the microcode update requires a host-level reboot versus a soft driver reload? We're trying to map impact against our telemetry and alerting.

Would like to avoid a scheduled window that hits our end-of-day job (03:40 UTC) if possible. If you can shift the disruptive steps earlier in the window, that would help.

— Ben Carter
Cloud Ops, Acme Corp

To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned capacity rebalancing & microcode security update — us-east4 (2026-08-03)

Looping in a short runbook excerpt and our mitigation plan for pinned replicas so we can respond to Acme's questions quickly.

High-level answers (internal):
- Pinned single-replica tasks: by default, our orchestrator will drain instances before eviction. For pinned replicas with hard affinity we will mark the instance as "do-not-evict" and perform microcode update during a later soft-swap if needed. If Acme wants to maintain strict pinning during the entire window we can schedule a node exclusion and avoid draining their lanes.
- Microcode update mode: host-level microcode application requires a reboot at the hypervisor level for some vendors. For the affected SKU set in us-east4 we've validated a microcode binary that needs a cold reboot of the host; that is the reason we're doing staggered rolling restarts.

Proposed concession: shift the most disruptive reboots to the start of the window (02:00–03:20 UTC) and run lower-risk pool swaps 03:20–05:00 UTC. That should avoid the 03:40 UTC EOD job Ben mentioned.

I'll prepare a short exemption ticket if Acme confirms they want strict pinning retained for the job window.

Marcus
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned capacity rebalancing & microcode security update — us-east4 (2026-08-03)

Ben — thanks for the quick reply and for flagging the EOD job. We reviewed internally and have: 

1) Shifted disruptive reboots to 02:00–03:20 UTC, lower-risk swaps run 03:20–05:00 UTC.
2) For your pinned replicas: we can apply a temporary exclusion for the specific node labels you provide and avoid evicting pinned processes. If you can share the node labels or the replica IDs by EOD 2026-08-02 we'll lock them out of the drain sequence.
3) Host-level microcode application requires a reboot for the SKUs affected in us-east4 (confirmed). We've minimized blast radius via staggered restarts and automatic rerouting.

We'll publish minute-by-minute updates on our status page during the window and will send a final post-maintenance note with a short postmortem and any customer-facing findings. See the operation runbook here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A_rebalance-plan (attached summary: status-page-notes.md).

If that plan works for Acme, no further action is needed on your side except the optional node labels.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: maintenance-window-params.csv (node-pool timing matrix), status-page-notes.md
